incidents.victim: 30,000+ Fortinet firewall/VPN users (govt, telecom, healthcare, defense)
incidents.vector: Mass credential harvesting and offline cracking of FortiGate config files and intercepted SSL VPN hashes, reusing leaked and unrotated admin credentials to log into exposed devices.
incidents.impact: A validated dataset of working admin/VPN credentials for ~73,932 FortiGate URLs across 194 countries was exposed; confirmed compromises include a Turkish NATO defense contractor from which classified documents were allegedly exfiltrated. Many affected devices remain online and unremediated.

incidents.attacker: Russia — financially motivated cybercrime group (Evil Corp)
incidents.vector: Law enforcement takedown of malware infrastructure that spread via fake browser/software update prompts on compromised (mostly WordPress) websites, serving as an initial-access broker for ransomware and espionage.
incidents.impact: Authorities from the Netherlands, Canada, U.S. and Germany seized 106 servers and disinfected nearly 15,000 hacked websites under Operation Endgame/Riptide, disrupting a long-running initial-access pipeline tied to multiple ransomware crews.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion and data theft, surfaced after the actor listed the company on its dark web leak portal.
incidents.impact: The ShinyHunters group claims to have stolen details of nearly 2.2 million customers; Kodak confirmed unauthorized access to its network but has not confirmed the scope.

incidents.victim: Salesforce customers via Klue Battlecards (Huntress, Recorded Future, others)
incidents.vector: Compromise of marketing vendor Klue via a long-disused but active credential, allowing attackers to harvest customer OAuth tokens and pull Salesforce data through the REST API.
incidents.impact: The Icarus extortion group exfiltrated business contacts, price quotes and sales data from multiple Salesforce instances and began extortion threats; the third such third-party-OAuth supply-chain attack after Salesloft Drift and Gainsight.

incidents.vector: Initial access via a high-privileged GitHub personal access token exposed in client-side JavaScript on an obscure subdomain, then used to clone private repos and harvest further credentials for lateral movement.
incidents.impact: Threat group FulcrumSec claims a ~2-month intrusion and theft of ~1.3TB (700,000+ files) including source code, drug R&D, clinical trial data and internal AI models, with a $25M ransom demand; data leaking began after non-payment. A second group (TheUSERS007) also claims a separate intrusion.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion (double extortion) into the IT environment of Australia's second-largest sugar producer.
incidents.impact: Two of the company's mills (Racecourse and Farleigh) were shut from June 10, halting harvesting across Queensland's Mackay region; the Gentlemen ransomware group claimed the attack and threatened to publish stolen data.

incidents.victim: Consumers running Android TV boxes (Popa/Vo1d botnet, ~1.5-2.5M IPs/day)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — proxy botnet & ad fraud
incidents.vector: Malicious/bundled SDKs on unofficial Android TV streaming boxes enroll home internet connections into a residential proxy network without meaningful user consent.
incidents.impact: Researchers linked the long-running Popa botnet — averaging 1.5-2.5 million IPs daily and used for ad fraud, account takeovers and mass data scraping — to NetNut, a proxy provider owned by Israeli firm Alarum Technologies, which disputes the findings.

incidents.victim: Open-source software ecosystem (npm, PyPI, GitHub, RubyGems)
incidents.vector: Compromise of maintainer credentials and CI/CD runners to inject malicious code into packages and propagate self-replicating Shai-Hulud worm variants downstream to automated build pipelines.
incidents.impact: TeamPCP has poisoned 1,000+ packages in under four months (516 malicious packages live, 3,000+ affected repos, 200+ compromised dev accounts), with variants tied to breaches at the European Commission, Mercor, LiteLLM, GitHub and Red Hat; researchers say GitHub dismissed related vulnerability reports.

incidents.vector: Breach of the agency's hunting and fishing license registration website.
incidents.impact: Personal details of more than 3 million people were stolen, including highly sensitive data such as government IDs, driver's licenses and home addresses; the agency has not disclosed when the breach occurred.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of legacy smart-contract functions in deprecated components that were never fully decommissioned.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole ~$1.34M from Raydium and ~$4.1M from Aztec Connect (hacked twice in one week); researchers note a coordinated campaign targeting legacy crypto contracts also hit DxSale this month.

incidents.vector: Takeover of the 'ehindero' npm maintainer account to publish poisoned package versions adding a malicious 'easy-day-js' typosquat of dayjs, which ran a postinstall dropper fetching a second-stage tasking implant.
incidents.impact: 140+ packages across the mastra/@mastra scopes were weaponized; any workstation or CI/CD pipeline running npm install/update was exposed to credential, token and build-environment theft. Packages were removed and attacker publish access revoked.

incidents.victim: Chinese citizens / crypto-asset holders (Silver Fox malware victims)
incidents.vector: Malspam and fake app/download sites delivering the Silver Fox (Winos) trojan, used to drop infostealers and custom RATs to steal funds and online assets.
incidents.impact: Chinese police arrested 67 suspects across five provinces tied to Silver Fox — the country's largest domestic cybercrime group — including the malware author and phishing-site operators, following a late-May CERT alert.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of critical FortiSandbox flaws CVE-2026-39808 (OS command injection) and CVE-2026-39813 (path traversal), patched in April, plus attempts on CVE-2026-25089.
incidents.impact: Researchers observed ~49 exploitation events from sources in nine countries; early reconnaissance/verification activity typically precedes a heavier wave. A FortiSandbox compromise grants elevated access within a trusted security appliance that connects to other Fortinet devices.

incidents.victim: Iranian banks (Bank Melli, Tejarat, Saderat, Export Development Bank)
incidents.vector: Attack reportedly targeting shared communications infrastructure used by the four banks.
incidents.impact: Online portals and mobile apps for four of Iran's largest banks were down over the weekend; the country's banking council said no customer data was accessed.

incidents.victim: FIFA (2026 World Cup broadcast & match systems)
incidents.vector: Broken access control in FIFA's Microsoft Entra tenant: client-side authorization with no server-side enforcement let a self-registered 'football agent' account reach privileged internal systems.
incidents.impact: An ethical hacker gained control over global World Cup TV stream production, match management (scores, start times), commentary and analytics systems; the flaw was reported via CISA/FBI and reportedly fixed the next day. No malicious exploitation observed.

incidents.vector: Historic Conti ransomware operation that hacked networks, encrypted data and used double-extortion against victims across 47 U.S. states and 31 countries (2020-2022).
incidents.impact: Ukrainian national Oleksii Lytvynenko pleaded guilty to wire fraud conspiracy after extradition from Ireland; Conti caused at least $150M in ransom payments. He faces up to 20 years in prison.

incidents.victim: U.S. security clearance holders & government/military employees
incidents.vector: Network of 13 fake 'consulting company' websites and job postings using AI-generated personas, stolen identities and encrypted apps to recruit clearance holders into sharing sensitive/classified information for payment.
incidents.impact: The DOJ and FBI seized 13 domains backed by suspected Chinese agents that targeted current and former U.S. clearance holders with sham consulting work, paying via crypto to obtain insider information.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS GlobalProtect users
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of CVE-2026-0257, an authentication bypass in PAN-OS GlobalProtect portal/gateway components, to initiate unauthorized VPN connections.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 observed an unidentified actor probing and, in a small portion of cases, establishing gateway-connected VPN sessions; no post-access lateral movement confirmed yet. The CVE was added to CISA's KEV catalog on May 29.
